correctness.rationale: For a0≠0 the linearization Δq(A) is separable and its roots form a d-dimensional Fq-space V. Its nonzero roots modulo the scalar subgroup μℓ correspond to the roots of G, via α↦α^ℓ, with the q-Frobenius action preserved. If A has a proper nonconstant factor D, Δq(D) has a proper nonzero root subspace in V (composition of linearizations gives Δq(A)), invariant under Frobenius, so that action cannot be transitive. If A is irreducible, the Frobenius action makes V a one-dimensional module over Fq[T]/(A); transitivity on V×/μℓ means that a root β of A has ord(β^ℓ)=n. For β=Γ^e, the joint conditions are gcd(e,n)=1 and e≡r mod q−1, by the norm formula and the constant's sign (-1)^d. Primes dividing both n and q−1 impose gcd(r,h)=1, while each other prime divisor of n forbids one class among the U possible progression indices; their square-free product divides U, so complete CRT cycles give the stated product. Every qualifying β has degree d since n≥U>q^(d−1), and its norm is constant over its d conjugates. Summing and using U≡d mod q−1 verifies the total and all-constants criterion, including q=2 (r=0 and h=1) and the empty product cases. Zero constant gives a reducible polynomial because n>1. Fresh direct tests of every polynomial in 12 small systems (268 polynomials including three systems over F4) passed, using gcds against X^(q^k)−X for all k≤n/2 rather than the cyclic-exponent formula. Replay: python /workspace/replay_frozen.py 5. These tests are finite corroboration; no formal proof check or expert attestation is claimed.
